evidence.explanation: This supports CoA-Z as a human investigational strategy for the PKAN branch of NBIA.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: CoA-Z targets the PKAN CoA-biosynthesis branch of NBIA pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: Subcutaneous nodules contain coiled adult worms and have an outer layer of fibrous scar and a central inflammatory cell exudate, which may cavitate.
evidence.explanation: Pathology review describes adult-worm encapsulation forming the fibrous subcutaneous nodule (onchocercoma).

steps/0.description: Adult Onchocerca volvulus worms coil and become encapsulated by host fibrous tissue in subcutaneous nodules (onchocercomata).

evidence.snippet: Onchocercal ocular disease covers a large spectrum of manifestations, which in severe cases, may lead to blindness.
evidence.explanation: Microfilarial invasion of ocular tissue underlies the spectrum of onchocercal ocular disease progressing to blindness.

steps/1.description: Onchocerca volvulus microfilariae migrate from subcutaneous nodules into the skin and anterior chamber of the eye. Their accumulation and death trigger host inflammatory responses causing dermatitis, hypopigmentation, and progressive ocular disease that can advance to blindness.

evidence.snippet: Onchocercal lymphadenitis is characterized initially by histiocytic hyperplasia and follicular atrophy and later by fibrosis and obstruction of lymph flow, a condition causing adenolymphocele ("hanging groin") and elephantiasis of the genitalia.
evidence.explanation: Pathology review describes progressive lymph node fibrosis and lymphatic obstruction culminating in the adenolymphocele ("hanging groin") deformity.

steps/2.description: Draining lymph nodes respond to microfilaria-driven chronic inflammation with histiocytic hyperplasia and follicular atrophy, progressing to fibrosis that obstructs lymph flow.

evidence.snippet: chemotherapeutic approach that targets filarial Wolbachia symbionts in the treatment and control of onchocerciasis, however, suggests that 100 mg/d of doxycycline for 6 weeks might be effective in reducing the filarial load and preventing ocular symptoms
evidence.explanation: Wolbachia endosymbionts are identified as a treatment target; doxycycline depletion reduces filarial load and prevents ocular symptoms.

steps/3.description: Onchocerca volvulus harbors obligate Wolbachia endosymbionts that support filarial survival and reproduction and contribute to the severity of host inflammatory pathology. Targeting Wolbachia with doxycycline depletes adult worms and reduces progression of ocular disease.

evidence.snippet: Skin symptoms are commonly nonspecific and include severe pruritus, acute and chronic dermatitis
evidence.explanation: Severe pruritus is described as a common skin symptom; author wording "commonly" maps to the FREQUENT band (no quantitative figure is given for the top VERY_FREQUENT band).

evidence.snippet: Skin symptoms are commonly nonspecific and include severe pruritus, acute and chronic dermatitis
evidence.explanation: Dermatitis is listed among the common skin symptoms; author wording "commonly" maps to the FREQUENT band.

evidence.snippet: Onchocercal ocular disease covers a large spectrum of manifestations, which in severe cases, may lead to blindness.
evidence.explanation: Severe ocular disease can lead to blindness.

evidence.snippet: vitiligo-like hypopigmentation, and atrophy
evidence.explanation: Vitiligo-like hypopigmentation is described as a characteristic skin manifestation of onchocerciasis.

steps/7.description: Vitiligo-like hypopigmentation with skin atrophy, a classic chronic skin manifestation of onchocerciasis sometimes called "leopard skin."

evidence.snippet: Individual microfilariae in the cornea may be associated with localized punctate lesions or, especially when present in large numbers, may provoke a sclerosing keratitis due to invasion by fibrovascular pannus from the limbal conjunctiva.
evidence.explanation: Human ocular-onchocerciasis pathology describes microfilarial invasion of the cornea provoking sclerosing keratitis, directly supporting keratitis as a corneal manifestation of onchocerciasis.

steps/8.description: Inflammatory keratitis caused by microfilarial invasion of the cornea, a leading cause of visual impairment in onchocerciasis.

evidence.snippet: Onchocerciasis is a major cause of blindness, and much of the blindness due to onchocerciasis is caused by chorioretinitis.
evidence.explanation: A longitudinal ophthalmologic study of onchocerciasis patients identifies chorioretinitis as the principal cause of onchocercal blindness.

steps/9.description: Posterior-segment inflammation of the choroid and retina; the leading cause of onchocercal blindness. Findings include intraretinal microfilariae, hemorrhages, pigmentary changes, and progressive chorioretinal scarring.

evidence.snippet: Subcutaneous nodules contain coiled adult worms and have an outer layer of fibrous scar and a central inflammatory cell exudate, which may cavitate.
evidence.explanation: Describes the subcutaneous nodule (onchocercoma) as a fibrous capsule enclosing coiled adult worms.

steps/10.description: Painless, palpable subcutaneous nodules containing encapsulated coiled adult Onchocerca volvulus worms, typically overlying bony prominences.

evidence.snippet: Onchocercal lymphadenitis is characterized initially by histiocytic hyperplasia and follicular atrophy and later by fibrosis and obstruction of lymph flow, a condition causing adenolymphocele ("hanging groin") and elephantiasis of the genitalia.
evidence.explanation: Describes progressive lymphatic fibrosis causing the adenolymphocele ("hanging groin") deformity.

steps/11.description: Adenolymphocele: enlarged, fibrotic inguinal or femoral lymph nodes that come to lie within a pendulous fold of lax, atrophic skin as a consequence of chronic onchocercal lymphadenitis; may be accompanied by elephantiasis of the genitalia.

edges/0.description: Microfilarial migration into the skin and the inflammatory response to dying microfilariae produce onchocercal dermatitis.

edges/1.description: The inflammatory reaction to microfilariae in the skin drives the severe itching characteristic of onchocerciasis.

edges/2.description: Chronic microfilaria-driven dermatitis leads to depigmentation ("leopard skin") changes.

edges/3.description: Microfilarial invasion of the cornea provokes inflammatory (sclerosing) keratitis.

edges/4.description: Microfilarial invasion and death within the choroid and retina provoke posterior-segment inflammation (chorioretinitis).

edges/5.description: Progressive ocular inflammation from microfilarial infiltration culminates in visual loss (river blindness).

edges/6.description: The chronic effects of onchocerciasis, including lymphadenitis, follow from ongoing microfilarial degeneration rather than from adult-worm encapsulation.

edges/7.description: Wolbachia endosymbiont products amplify the corneal inflammatory response that drives sclerosing keratitis.

edges/8.description: Wolbachia-driven inflammatory pathology contributes to posterior-segment chorioretinitis.

edges/9.description: Wolbachia-driven inflammatory pathology contributes to progression of onchocercal ocular disease toward blindness.

edges/10.description: Encapsulation of coiled adult worms in an outer layer of fibrous scar forms the palpable subcutaneous nodule.

edges/11.description: Progressive lymphatic fibrosis and obstruction of lymph flow produces adenolymphocele ("hanging groin") and genital elephantiasis.

evidence.snippet: Ivermectin is, at present, the drug of choice for skin and ocular manifestations.
evidence.explanation: The abstract identifies ivermectin as the drug of choice.

treatments/0.description: Ivermectin (a macrocyclic lactone) is the drug of choice for skin and ocular manifestations of onchocerciasis. It kills microfilariae and is used in mass drug administration programs for disease control and elimination.

evidence.snippet: In 2018, the US Food and Drug Administration approved the macrocylic lactone moxidectin (MOX) at 8 mg dosage for onchocerciasis treatment in individuals aged ≥12 years.
evidence.explanation: Documents FDA approval of moxidectin 8 mg for onchocerciasis treatment in 2018.

treatments/1.description: Moxidectin is an FDA-approved macrocyclic lactone for onchocerciasis treatment in individuals aged 12 years and older (8 mg single oral dose, approved 2018), offering an alternative to ivermectin with a more sustained microfilaricidal effect.

evidence.snippet: 100 mg/d of doxycycline for 6 weeks might be effective in reducing the filarial load and preventing ocular symptoms
evidence.explanation: Describes anti-Wolbachia effect of doxycycline in reducing filarial load and preventing ocular disease progression.

treatments/2.description: A 6-week course of doxycycline 100 mg/day targets the obligate Wolbachia endosymbionts of Onchocerca volvulus. Wolbachia depletion is macrofilaricidal (sterilizes adult females) and reduces filarial load and ocular disease progression.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Doxycycline depletes the obligate Wolbachia endosymbionts, which is macrofilaricidal and reduces filarial load and progression of ocular disease.

evidence.snippet: Dermal fibroblasts from most individuals with osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) type I produce about half the normal amount of type I procollagen, as a result of decreased synthesis of one of its constituent chains, pro alpha 1 (I).
evidence.explanation: Landmark paper demonstrating that OI type I results from 50% reduced type I procollagen synthesis due to diminished pro alpha 1(I) chain production.

evidence.snippet: COL1A1 haploinsufficiency mutations lead to the mildest form of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), OI type I.
evidence.explanation: Large clinical study (86 patients) confirming that COL1A1 haploinsufficiency specifically causes the mild type I phenotype.

steps/1.description: Null mutations in COL1A1 (nonsense, frameshift, splice site mutations causing nonsense-mediated mRNA decay) result in ~50% reduction in type I collagen production. The collagen that is produced has normal structure, explaining the milder phenotype compared to dominant-negative structural mutations.

evidence.snippet: Type I osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a dominantly inherited disease characterized clinically by bone fractures during childhood, blue sclerae, and frequent hearing loss accompanied by a decreased content of type I collagen in bone and skin.
evidence.explanation: Landmark type I OI study identifying blue sclerae as part of the classic clinical phenotype.

steps/2.description: Blue sclerae are a classic extraskeletal sign of osteogenesis imperfecta type I.

evidence.snippet: The average rate of long-bone fracture (femur, tibia/fibula, humerus, radius/ulna) in pediatric patients was 0.62 fractures per year, one-half of which affected the tibia/fibula. Long-bone fracture rate was negatively associated with age and lumbar spine areal bone mineral density.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies fracture rate in COL1A1 haploinsufficiency patients and confirms that fracture frequency decreases with age.

steps/3.description: Recurrent long-bone fractures are a core skeletal manifestation, and fracture rate declines with age.

evidence.snippet: Vertebral compression fractures were observed in 71% of the 58 pediatric patients who had lateral spine radiographs.
evidence.explanation: This cohort shows that vertebral compression fractures are a frequent and clinically important component of the type I OI skeletal phenotype.

steps/4.description: Vertebral compression fractures are frequent in growing patients with COL1A1 haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: Scoliosis was present in about 30% of pediatric patients but the Cobb angle was <30 degrees in all cases.
evidence.explanation: Supports scoliosis as an occasional and usually mild spinal manifestation in pediatric type I OI.

steps/5.description: Mild scoliosis occurs in a substantial minority of pediatric patients.

evidence.snippet: It was found that the most common age of onset was in the second, third and fourth decades of life. At the age of 50 approximately 50 per cent of the patients had symptoms of hearing impairment; over the next 20 years there was little further increase. Differences were shown between patients with different clinical types of osteogenesis imperfecta as delineated in the Sillence classification; hearing loss was significantly less common in the type IV disease than in the type I disorder.
evidence.explanation: Large OI survey showing typical adult onset of hearing impairment and demonstrating that hearing loss is more common in type I than in type IV disease.

steps/6.description: Progressive hearing impairment usually begins in adulthood, with onset most often in the second to fourth decades.

evidence.snippet: RESULTS: A total of ten patients had abnormal discolourations referable to DI: four patients were affected by OI type I, three patients by OI type III, and three patients by OI type IV.
evidence.explanation: Pediatric cohort directly documenting dentinogenesis imperfecta in children with type I OI.

steps/7.description: Dentinogenesis imperfecta can occur in a subset of children with osteogenesis imperfecta type I.

evidence.snippet: The average final height Z-score was -1.1, representing a deficit of 8 to 10 cm compared to the general population.
evidence.explanation: COL1A1 haploinsufficiency cohort of 86 patients showing a modest but consistent height deficit, confirming mild rather than severe short stature in OI type I.

steps/8.description: Adults with OI type I have mildly reduced stature, averaging approximately 8–10 cm shorter than the general population (height Z-score approximately −1.1), though near-normal stature is preserved relative to the more severe OI types caused by structural collagen mutations.

evidence.snippet: Mobility aids including orthotics to stabilize lax joints.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management section references lax joints as a clinical feature in COL1A1/COL1A2-related OI requiring orthotic stabilization.

steps/9.description: Joint laxity is an extraskeletal feature of type I collagen deficiency, arising from reduced collagen content in ligaments and joint capsules. Symptomatic lax joints are managed with orthotics and mobility aids.

evidence.snippet: HP:0002645 | Wormian bones | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists Wormian bones as an occasional feature of the OI spectrum, consistent with their recognised occurrence across OI types including type I. The row is cited for the association only. No type I-specific frequency is asserted, because ORPHA:666 measures the whole OI spectrum rather than type I alone and no narrower source quantifies the finding in type I.

evidence.snippet: Of the radiographs analysed, platybasia, basilar impression, basilar invagination, and the presence of Wormian bones, could not be evaluated in 71 (22.3%), 48 (15.2%), 61 (19.5%) and 28 (9.4%) radiographs respectively
evidence.explanation: This NHS England specialist OI service study systematically assessed Wormian bones on skull radiographs across OI subtypes, establishing them as a routinely monitored cranial finding in OI. The quoted sentence reports how many radiographs were non-evaluable rather than the occurrence of Wormian bones, so it supports the finding's clinical relevance but does not quantify its frequency. Neither source measures type I alone, so this record carries no frequency band.

steps/10.description: Wormian (sutural) bones are accessory intrasutural ossification centres visible on skull radiographs. They are a recognised radiographic finding in the OI spectrum, including in milder type I cases.

evidence.snippet: HP:0000939 | Osteoporosis | Frequent (79-30%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists osteoporosis as a frequent feature of the OI spectrum, consistent with the well-established low bone mass in type I. The row is cited for the association only. No type I-specific frequency is asserted, because ORPHA:666's band is measured over the whole OI spectrum — in which the severe types carry most of the burden — and the COL1A1 cohort cited below reports a BMD-fracture correlation rather than an occurrence rate.

evidence.snippet: Long-bone fracture rate was negatively associated with age and lumbar spine areal bone mineral density.
evidence.explanation: The inverse relationship between fracture rate and lumbar spine BMD in this COL1A1 haploinsufficiency cohort directly reflects the low bone mass underlying the osteoporotic phenotype in OI type I.

steps/11.description: Reduced bone mass meeting the threshold for osteoporosis is documented in adults with OI type I, reflecting the underlying 50% deficit in type I collagen production.

evidence.snippet: HP:0000978 | Bruising susceptibility | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists bruising susceptibility as an occasional feature across the OI spectrum, supporting its occurrence in type I. The band itself is not adopted: it is measured over the whole spectrum, and PMID:6822598 below states that bruising is *more* common in type I than in type IV, so the spectrum band may understate type I rather than describe it. No type I-specific rate is available, so this record carries no frequency band.

evidence.snippet: In Type 4 the first fracture more commonly occurs at birth, dentinogenesis imperfecta is more frequent than in Type 1 and bruising and nose-bleeds are less common.
evidence.explanation: This type I versus type IV comparison explicitly states that bruising and nose-bleeds are more common in type I than in type IV, confirming bruising susceptibility as a feature of type I OI.

steps/12.description: Easy bruising is a recognised extraskeletal feature of OI type I, more prominent than in type IV. It reflects deficient type I collagen in skin and subcutaneous connective tissue.

evidence.snippet: HP:0002653 | Bone pain | Frequent (79-30%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists bone pain as a frequent feature of OI, consistent with its clinical prominence in adults with type I. The row is cited for the association only. No type I-specific frequency is asserted, because ORPHA:666's band is measured over the whole OI spectrum and the stakeholder study cited below names pain as a priority concern without reporting an occurrence rate.

evidence.snippet: Other areas included pain, gastrointestinal problems, mental health, nutrition, menopause/pregnancy, and basilar invagination.
evidence.explanation: This OI community stakeholder study identifies pain as a primary concern of adults with OI, emphasising that it is under-studied and undertreated across all OI types including type I.

steps/13.description: Chronic or recurrent bone pain is reported by adults with OI type I and is among the most frequently cited unmet clinical concerns in this population.

evidence.snippet: HP:0000975 | Hyperhidrosis | Frequent (79-30%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists hyperhidrosis as a frequent feature of the OI spectrum, supporting its occurrence in type I OI. No type I-specific frequency is asserted here because the Orphanet band reflects the whole OI spectrum rather than type I alone.

steps/14.description: Increased sweating is reported in a substantial minority of OI patients. It arises from altered connective-tissue and autonomic thermoregulatory responses related to type I collagen deficiency.

evidence.snippet: HP:0001730 | Progressive hearing impairment | Frequent (79-30%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists progressive hearing impairment as a frequent feature of OI. The band is measured over the whole OI spectrum, so it is cited here for the association rather than as the source of the type I band; the FREQUENT band retained below rests on PMID:11276328, which measures the rate directly and shows type I at the upper end of the spectrum.

evidence.snippet: It was found that the most common age of onset was in the second, third and fourth decades of life. At the age of 50 approximately 50 per cent of the patients had symptoms of hearing impairment; over the next 20 years there was little further increase.
evidence.explanation: This large survey of 1,394 OI patients demonstrates the progressive trajectory of hearing loss in type I OI, plateauing at about 50% by age 50. The measured ~50% rate is what the FREQUENT (30-79%) band on this record rests on, rather than the OI-spectrum ORPHA:666 row above.

evidence.snippet: hearing loss was significantly less common in the type IV disease than in the type I disorder
evidence.explanation: The same survey breaks its cohort down by Sillence type and places type I above type IV, so the pooled rate is a conservative floor for type I rather than a spectrum band imported into a milder subtype.

steps/15.description: Hearing loss in OI type I is typically progressive, beginning in the second to fourth decade and advancing over subsequent decades.

evidence.snippet: In each case there was marked diminution in steady-state mRNA levels from one COL1A1 allele. Loss of an allele through deletion or rearrangement was not the cause of the diminished COL1A1 mRNA levels.
evidence.explanation: Study of 23 individuals from 21 families showed null allele-associated mRNA reduction, establishing the molecular basis of COL1A1 haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of the COL1A1 and COL1A2 genes by PCR amplification and scanning by conformation-sensitive gel electrophoresis identifies only COL1A1 mutations in 15 patients with osteogenesis imperfecta type I.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that OI type I is specifically associated with COL1A1 mutations, with common null-allele mutation sequences identified.

genes/0.notes: Heterozygous null mutations in COL1A1 account for most OI type I cases. These include nonsense mutations, frameshift mutations, and splice site mutations that lead to nonsense-mediated decay of the mutant transcript. The 50% reduction in collagen quantity produces a milder phenotype than structural mutations.

evidence.snippet: Bisphosphonates continue to be used most extensively in those with vertebral fractures, frequent long bone fractures, or more severe OI.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews notes bisphosphonate use is most strongly indicated for patients with vertebral or frequent fractures, applying a severity-based threshold rather than prescribing universally for mild OI.

treatments/0.description: Bisphosphonate therapy is used in OI type I primarily in those with vertebral fractures or frequent long-bone fractures; evidence for fracture reduction is less robust in mild OI than in severe forms. Benefit is most clearly established for improving bone mineral density in children.

treatments/1.description: Exercise and physical therapy to strengthen muscles and improve mobility while protecting fragile bones.

evidence.snippet: Fractures are treated with as short a period of immobility as is practical, small and lightweight casts, and physical therapy as soon as casts are removed; intramedullary rodding when indicated to provide anatomic positioning of limbs; bracing of limbs depending on OI severity.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes the standard conservative fracture management approach and the criteria for intramedullary rodding in OI type I.

treatments/2.description: Most fractures in OI type I are managed conservatively with casting, splinting, and brief immobilization. Intramedullary rodding is reserved for recurrent long-bone fractures causing deformity.

evidence.snippet: The overall rate of mosaicism is up to 16% in the parents of children with COL1A1/COL1A2-OI. Each child of an individual with COL1A1/COL1A2-OI has a 50% chance of inheriting the causative variant.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews quantifies key recurrence risk figures: up to 16% parental mosaicism rate and 50% transmission risk per child, supporting the counseling description.

treatments/3.description: Genetic counseling is recommended given autosomal dominant inheritance. Approximately 60% of probands with mild OI have de novo mutations; each child of an affected individual has a 50% chance of inheriting the causative variant. Parental mosaicism occurs in up to 16% of apparently unaffected parents, influencing recurrence risk estimation.

evidence.snippet: Conductive hearing loss may be improved with middle ear surgery; standard treatments for later-onset sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies audiological management for progressive hearing loss affecting approximately 50% of OI type I patients by age 50.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 50 approximately 50 per cent of the patients had symptoms of hearing impairment; over the next 20 years there was little further increase.
evidence.explanation: Population study of 1,394 OI patients quantifying hearing impairment prevalence and onset, informing the audiological surveillance schedule.

treatments/4.description: Hearing evaluation every three years from age five until hearing loss is identified, then as indicated. Approximately 50% of adults with OI type I develop hearing impairment by age 50. Conductive hearing loss may improve with middle-ear surgery; sensorineural or mixed hearing loss is managed with standard audiological care and hearing aids.

evidence.snippet: Dental care to maintain both primary and permanent dentition, a functional bite or occlusion, optimal gingival health, and overall appearance.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies dental care goals for COL1A1/COL1A2-related OI, with frequency based on dentinogenesis imperfecta status.

treatments/5.description: Dental examination every six months beginning in early childhood for those with or at risk for dentinogenesis imperfecta; annual exams for those without DI. Goals include maintaining dentition, functional occlusion, gingival health, and appearance.

evidence.snippet: The scarcity of animal and cell models has also contributed to the lack of initiatives to explore osteogenesis imperfecta type 1. This Review aims to break this vicious cycle of osteogenesis imperfecta type 1 obscurity by defining knowledge gaps that future investigations of this disease should aim to address.
evidence.explanation: The review identifies inadequate disease models and mechanistic knowledge gaps as barriers to understanding OI Type 1 pathophysiology.

open_questions/0.rationale: The OI Type 1 entry models the 50% quantitative collagen reduction as a single haploinsufficiency state. Recent clinical reviews identify the precise dose-response relationship between COL1A1 reduction and phenotype severity as an unresolved mechanistic question. The distinction between absolute collagen levels and downstream bone pathophysiology remains under-characterized, and the lack of adequate animal and cellular models has limited investigation of this quantitative relationship.

evidence.snippet: WNT1 is a secreted signaling protein that binds the frizzled receptor (FZD) and the coreceptor low-density lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5).
evidence.explanation: Defines WNT1 as a secreted ligand acting through FZD and the LRP5 coreceptor, the signaling axis disrupted in OI type XV.

evidence.snippet: Initial functional analysis revealed that altered WNT1 proteins fail to activate canonical LRP5-mediated WNT-regulated β-catenin signaling.
evidence.explanation: Documents that disease-causing WNT1 proteins fail to activate canonical LRP5-mediated WNT/beta-catenin signaling, the proximal molecular defect.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to wild type WNT1, WNT1C218G and WNT1S295* did not induce significant accumulation of non-phosphorylated or total β-catenin in either cytosolic or nuclear fractions
evidence.explanation: Shows mutant WNT1 fails to drive beta-catenin accumulation, confirming loss of canonical WNT signaling output.

steps/1.description: WNT1 is a secreted signaling protein that binds the Frizzled receptor (FZD) and the coreceptor LRP5/6 to activate canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling. Biallelic loss-of-function or hypofunctional WNT1 variants (frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, missense) yield WNT1 protein that fails to activate canonical LRP5-mediated WNT-regulated beta-catenin signaling, so beta-catenin does not accumulate to induce WNT target genes. This places OI type XV mechanistically apart from the collagen-defect OI types: the proximal lesion is failure of an osteoanabolic signaling ligand rather than a defect in type I collagen.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, osteoblasts cultured in vitro showed enhanced Wnt1 expression with advancing differentiation, indicating a role of WNT1 in osteoblast function and bone development.
evidence.explanation: Links WNT1 to osteoblast differentiation and bone development, the program impaired when WNT1 signaling is lost.

evidence.snippet: These assays demonstrate the markedly diminished capacity of the abnormal proteins to induce canonical WNT signaling and associated osteoblast differentiation.
evidence.explanation: Functional assays confirm that mutant WNT1 impairs canonical WNT signaling and the associated osteoblast differentiation.

steps/2.description: Canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling drives osteoblast differentiation and bone formation; WNT1 expression rises as osteoblasts differentiate, indicating a role for WNT1 in osteoblast function and bone development. With WNT1 signaling lost, WNT target-gene induction and osteoblast-mediated mineralization are reduced, so the osteoanabolic bone-formation program cannot proceed normally.

evidence.snippet: Radiographs of both affected children showed severe osteopenia with multiple fractures and sequelae over time, including vertebral compression fractures, resultant kyphoscoliosis, severe short stature, and long bone deformities
evidence.explanation: Documents the low-bone-mass, multiple-fracture, deformity phenotype that results from impaired WNT1-driven bone formation.

evidence.snippet: In vitro, aberrant forms of the WNT1 protein showed impaired capacity to induce canonical WNT signaling, their target genes, and mineralization.
evidence.explanation: Connects loss of WNT1 signaling to impaired target-gene induction and mineralization, the cellular basis of the reduced bone mass.

steps/3.description: The deficit in WNT-driven osteoblast bone formation and mineralization produces low bone mineral density and impaired bone quality, manifesting clinically as reduced bone mass, recurrent low-impact fractures, vertebral compression, growth deficiency, and progressive long-bone deformity. In affected children, radiographs show severe osteopenia with multiple fractures and sequelae including vertebral compression fractures, kyphoscoliosis, severe short stature, and long-bone deformities.

edges/1.description: Loss of canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling impairs osteoblast differentiation and the osteoanabolic activity needed for bone formation and mineralization.

edges/2.description: Deficient osteoblast-mediated bone formation and mineralization yield low bone mass and a mechanically weak skeleton prone to fracture and deformity.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe four recessive-OI-affected families in which we identified causative mutations in wingless-type MMTV integration site family 1 (WNT1).
evidence.explanation: Identifies WNT1 as the causative gene in recessive OI (type XV) across four families.

evidence.snippet: In a separate family with 2 siblings affected by recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, we identified a homozygous nonsense mutation, c.884C→A, p.Ser295*.

evidence.snippet: In consanguineous families, we identified five homozygous mutations in WNT1: one frameshift mutation, two missense mutations, one splice-site mutation, and one nonsense mutation.

evidence.snippet: Bisphosphonates continue to be used most extensively in those with vertebral fractures, frequent long bone fractures, or more severe OI.

evidence.snippet: All cases of PMC and HBC demonstrated nuclear reactivity for FOXL2 in the subepithelial stromal cells. Ninety percent of MEST demonstrated nuclear FOXL2 positivity. evidence.snippet: Mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs) are rare pancreas tumors distinguished from intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) by the presence of ovarian-type stroma.

evidence.snippet: MCNs frequently harbored KRAS mutations, at rates of 100% in HG/INV lesions and 50% in LG lesions of HG/INV and LG cases.

evidence.snippet: The frequency of RNF43 mutations was significantly higher in HG/INV cases than in LG cases. Furthermore, HG/INV lesions (56%) and LG lesions (33%) of HG/INV cases possessed RNF43 mutation, whereas no such mutation was detected in any LG cases.

evidence.snippet: KRAS, GNAS, RNF43 and PIK3CA were sequenced in 25 surgical cases of hepatopancreatic MCN. evidence.snippet: We also discuss the most prevalent genetic alterations in these precancerous lesions, including somatic mutations in the oncogenes KRAS and GNAS as well as tumour suppressor genes CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4.

evidence.snippet: Impaired peroxisome biogenesis, including defects of membrane assembly, import of peroxisomal matrix proteins, and division of peroxisome, causes peroxisome biogenesis disorders (PBDs).

evidence.explanation: Establishes that PEX19 carries two separable jobs, cytosolic stabilisation of newly made membrane proteins and receptor-mediated delivery, so its loss removes both at once rather than only the targeting step this node is named for.

steps/2.description: Pex19p is a soluble protein, mostly cytosolic at steady state, that binds a broad range of peroxisomal membrane proteins through the regions those proteins use for peroxisomal targeting, and delivers them to the membrane. Farnesylation of its C-terminal CaaX motif reorganises the cargo-binding surface and strengthens the interaction, which is why alleles truncating that region are inactivating. When Pex19p is absent, newly synthesised membrane proteins are degraded or delivered to mitochondria instead.

evidence.snippet: Pathogenic mutations in PEX3, PEX16 and PEX19 cause affected cells to be devoid of peroxisomes

evidence.snippet: the genes PEX 1, 2, 5-7, 10, 11β, 12-14 and 26 are essential for the import of matrix enzymes from the cytosol into peroxisomes, and PEX 3, 16, and 19 work for the biogenesis of peroxisomes and assembly of peroxisomal membranes

steps/3.description: Cells from complementation group J contain no peroxisomal membrane remnants. evidence.snippet: HsPEX19 expression also restored peroxisomal protein import in fibroblasts from a patient (PBDJ-01) with Zellweger syndrome of CG-J.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, Pex19p is apparently involved at the initial stage in peroxisome membrane assembly, before the import of matrix protein.
evidence.explanation: States the ordering this node depends on: membrane assembly first, matrix import after.

steps/4.description: With no peroxisomal compartment, matrix enzymes remain in the cytosol, where they are degraded or left in unprocessed precursor form. Expressing wild-type PEX19 in group-J patient fibroblasts restores matrix protein import, which is what demonstrates that the matrix defect is downstream of the PEX19 lesion rather than a separate one.

steps/5.description: The first steps of ether-lipid synthesis are peroxisomal, so plasmalogens fall when the compartment is lost. In Zellweger fibroblasts the plasmalogen fraction of phosphatidylethanolamine is roughly half of control while total phospholipid content and membrane fluidity are unchanged, so this is a selective lipid defect rather than general membrane damage.

edges/1.description: Loss of functional Pex19p removes the cytosolic receptor that peroxisomal membrane proteins depend on.

evidence.snippet: Although these peroxins have been extensively studied, no consensus has been reached yet on how they operate.
evidence.explanation: States that the Pex3/Pex19 mechanism is unresolved, which is why this edge is left as a dependency rather than being decomposed into named steps.

evidence.snippet: Here, we discuss two major models of their function, namely, in direct insertion of proteins into the peroxisomal membrane or in formation of PMP‐containing vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
evidence.explanation: Names the two competing models, so a reader can see what the unnamed intermediate step would have to choose between.

edges/2.description: With no route for membrane proteins to reach a peroxisomal membrane, no such membrane is assembled. Kept DIRECT deliberately. Pex19p hands its cargo off at the membrane in partnership with Pex3p, so a named intermediate could be written in here - but which step that partnership performs is genuinely unsettled, with direct insertion into the peroxisomal membrane and budding of PMP-containing vesicles from the ER both still live models. Naming one would assert a mechanism the field has not agreed on; the edge records the dependency and this note records the dispute.

edges/3.description: A matrix cannot be imported into a compartment that does not exist, so matrix import fails as a consequence of the membrane defect rather than in parallel with it.

edges/4.description: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation is lost with the matrix enzymes that carry it out.

edges/5.description: Ether-lipid synthesis begins in the peroxisome and fails with it.

edges/6.description: The dysmorphic and bone findings are consistently reported across the Zellweger spectrum and in the PEX19 cases specifically, but which metabolic arm produces them is not established, so this edge is drawn from the loss of peroxisomal function as a whole rather than from a named metabolite.

edges/7.description: Congenital malformations are part of the severe Zellweger phenotype and renal and cardiac defects were present in the reported PEX19 patients, but no mechanistic route from peroxisome loss to these particular malformations has been established; the edge records the association, not a worked-out mechanism.

edges/8.description: Liver disease is a core component of the severe Zellweger phenotype and developed in the longest-surviving reported PEX19 patient.

edges/9.description: Neuronal migration defects are a defining congenital malformation of the severe end of the spectrum.

edges/10.description: Plasmalogen loss is one of the two metabolic arms conventionally invoked for the brain phenotype of the Zellweger spectrum. No study cited here isolates its contribution in PEX19 disease specifically.

edges/17.description: GeneReviews reports the poor feeding of the affected newborn in the same breath as the hypotonia, so it is placed here rather than as an independent gastrointestinal finding.

genes/0.notes: PEX19 encodes the 299-residue cytosolic chaperone and import receptor for peroxisomal membrane proteins, with three conserved domains and a C-terminal CAAX box that is farnesylated. Reported disease alleles include truncating variants at both ends of the severity range and missense variants associated with late-onset, mildly affected, long-surviving patients, so genotype does track phenotype to some degree within this gene.

steps/1.description: Both PEX2 alleles are altered, but the genotype as a whole leaves partial peroxin-2 activity. Two configurations are reported at this end of the series: homozygosity for a frameshift so close to the stop codon that most of the protein survives (c.865_866insA, p.Ser289LysfsX36), and compound heterozygosity for a residual-function missense allele opposite a nonsense allele already known from classic Zellweger syndrome (E55K opposite R119X). The residual-function threshold, not gene identity, is what separates this entry from peroxisome biogenesis disorder 5A.

evidence.snippet: PBD patients belonging to complementation group 10 (CG10) have mutations in the PEX2 gene (PXMP3), which codes for a protein (PEX2) that contains two transmembrane domains and a zinc-binding domain considered to be important for its interaction with other proteins of the peroxisomal protein import machinery.

evidence.snippet: The PEX2, PEX10 and PEX12 genes encode peroxins that are integral peroxisomal membrane proteins with a cytosolic carboxy-terminal RING finger domain that act as ubiquitin ligases required for the ubiquitination of the PTS1-receptor (PEX5) in the peroxisomal membrane
evidence.explanation: Names the ligase activity and its substrate. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL with quote_role BACKGROUND: the sentence is the discussion's framing of established biochemistry rather than a result of the case report it sits in.

evidence.snippet: Recycling requires receptor modification by a membrane-embedded ubiquitin ligase complex comprising three RING finger domain-containing proteins (Pex2, Pex10 and Pex12)
evidence.explanation: The complex peroxin-2's RING domain belongs to, and what it does. INDIRECT because the structure was solved in a fungal system, so the human claim rests on conservation.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, a defect in the C-terminal portion of Pex2p exposed to the cytosol containing a RING finger motif caused the mild phenotype, residual enzyme activities, and mosaic detectable peroxisomes in fibroblasts from the patient.
evidence.explanation: The single sentence that ties the defining claims of this entry together at the PEX2 locus: a C-terminal RING-region lesion, a mild clinical phenotype, residual enzyme activity, and peroxisomal mosaicism. It is also the structural account of why the c.865_866insA frameshift seventeen codons from the stop codon lands in this band.

steps/2.description: Peroxin-2 is an integral peroxisomal membrane protein with two transmembrane domains and a cytosolic C-terminal zinc-binding RING finger. Together with peroxin-10 and peroxin-12 it forms the membrane-embedded ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates the PTS1 receptor PEX5 so the receptor can be retrotranslocated and reused. Degrading that activity rather than abolishing it is the molecular difference between this entry and the severe band.

evidence.snippet: Catalase-less peroxisomes were also observed in human fibroblasts from patients with milder forms of peroxisome biogenesis disorder, including the one from which the mutant PEX2 gene was derived.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the partially functional organelle characterised in the cell model is present in patient fibroblasts, including the PEX2 patient whose allele was used.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence microscopy analysis using antibodies raised against catalase, a peroxisomal matrix enzyme, revealed a heterogeneous pattern: some cells showed normal peroxisomes whereas in other cells peroxisomes were absent, and in yet other cells a mixed picture was observed.
evidence.explanation: Peroxisomal mosaicism observed directly in a PEX2 patient's fibroblasts, which is the cellular claim of this node.

evidence.snippet: We found that all IRD cell lines and some NALD lines belonging to several different complementation groups are temperature-sensitive in peroxisome assembly; that is, they lacked catalase-positive peroxisomes at 37 degrees C, but do gain the peroxisomes at 30 degrees C.
evidence.explanation: The temperature-sensitive behaviour of the mild band's import defect, from the study that identified the PEX2 E55K/R119X genotype in an infantile Refsum disease patient.

evidence.snippet: Some of the fibroblasts from the patient with the del642G mutation contained numerous catalase-containing particles, whereas no fibroblasts containing such particles were found in the patient with the del550C mutation.
evidence.explanation: The cell-by-cell contrast between a mild and a severe PEX2 allele in the same study: catalase-containing particles in some fibroblasts of the C-terminal-lesion patient and in none of the other. This is the observation the word mosaicism names.

evidence.snippet: The mosaicism was observed both at 37°C and at 40°C.
evidence.explanation: Cited against the generality of the temperature-sensitive claim rather than against the node. In this PEX2 patient the mosaicism did not resolve with temperature, so a negative temperature-shift assay does not exclude a mild PEX2 genotype - which is why the same report concludes that sequencing the PEX genes was necessary.

steps/3.description: Matrix-protein import is reduced but not abolished. In patient fibroblasts this appears as peroxisomal mosaicism - some cells with normal peroxisomes, some with none, some mixed - and as a population of partially functional organelles that import the PTS1 enzymes acyl-CoA oxidase and thiolase while leaving catalase in the cytosol, which the group that described them named catalase-less peroxisomes. In the PEX2 E55K case the defect is temperature-sensitive, recovering at a permissive temperature; in the Italian patient the mosaicism persisted at 40 degrees, so the temperature test does not detect every mild PEX2 genotype. The fibroblast bound below is the cell the defect was assayed in, not a claim about which cell drives the disease: the import machinery is ubiquitous and the tissue that fails clinically is the cerebellum.

evidence.snippet: showed normal plasmalogen biosynthesis, DHAP-AT activity, oxidation of VLCFAs, and pristanic acid
evidence.explanation: The fibroblast result in the ataxic form. Quoted because it is the strongest single statement of how attenuated this node is here; the same paragraph adds that phytanic acid oxidation was only slightly abnormal.

evidence.snippet: DHAPAT activity and C26:0 beta-oxidation, which are considered the best biochemical markers in predicting life expectancy of patients with PBDs (Gootjes et al. 2002), were normal.
evidence.explanation: An independent patient with the same result, and the prognostic reading the authors put on it.

steps/4.description: Beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, alpha-oxidation of phytanic acid, beta-oxidation of the C27 bile-acid intermediates and the first steps of plasmalogen synthesis all depend on imported matrix enzymes, so all are affected together - but at this end of the series they are affected partially. In the ataxic brothers fibroblast plasmalogen synthesis, DHAPAT activity and very-long-chain fatty acid oxidation were normal and only phytanic acid alpha-oxidation was slightly abnormal; in the Italian patient DHAPAT activity and C26:0 beta-oxidation were likewise normal. This is the node where this entry diverges most sharply from classic Zellweger syndrome, and it is the reason a fibroblast panel can be reassuring in a patient who has the disease.

evidence.snippet: Nerve conduction studies indicated a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.explanation: The electrophysiological basis for calling the neuropathy axonal and sensorimotor, which is what the phenotype binding asserts.

evidence.snippet: Fundoscopic examination, electroretinogram, EEG, electromyography, peripheral nerve conduction, visual, brainstem auditory and somatosensory evoked potentials, and audiogram were normal at 9 and 14 years.
evidence.explanation: A negative result recorded as such. In the two ataxic brothers nerve conduction, retinal and auditory testing were all normal into the mid-teens, so neither the neuropathy nor the sensory loss is obligatory in this entry, and their absence does not argue against the diagnosis.

steps/5.description: Length-dependent axonal degeneration of peripheral nerve, established on nerve conduction studies. It is a second, largely independent site of injury rather than a consequence of the cerebellar lesion, and its severity does not track the ataxia: the Sevin brothers had normal nerve conduction at nine, fourteen and eighteen years, while the older Italian patient had a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with pes cavus.

evidence.snippet: Plasma VLCFAs were nearly normal in patients P1 and P2, but a moderate increase in the levels of phytanic and pristanic acids was found, prompting us to suspect a peroxisomal disorder
evidence.explanation: The selective, attenuated pattern this node asserts, and the analytes that actually led to the diagnosis in the ataxic form.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of plasma peroxisomal parameters revealed increased levels of very long chain fatty acids (VLCFAs), branched-chain fatty acids (pristanic and phytanic acid), and bile acid intermediates, prompting us to suspect a peroxisomal disorder.
evidence.explanation: An unrelated patient in whom the very-long-chain fatty acids were raised, which is why this node describes the pattern as variable between patients rather than as a fixed signature.

steps/6.description: The circulating biochemical lesion. At this end of the spectrum it is attenuated and selective: in the ataxic brothers plasma very-long-chain fatty acids were nearly normal while phytanic and pristanic acid were moderately raised, whereas in the Italian patient very-long-chain fatty acids, branched-chain fatty acids and bile-acid intermediates were all raised and erythrocyte plasmalogens were normal. Which analytes move therefore differs between reported patients, and a single normal analyte carries little exclusionary weight.

evidence.snippet: Cerebellar defects (cerebellar hypoplasia, altered folial pattern, abnormal Purkinje cell dendritic arborization) are observed in PEX 2 deficient mice
evidence.explanation: The only evidence that the cerebellar lesion of PEX2 deficiency is Purkinje-centered, and the basis for conforming this node to the Purkinje degeneration module. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the quoted finding is from PEX2-null mice, and BACKGROUND because this human case report is restating a mouse result it did not generate. INDIRECT: a null mouse is a more severe lesion than the residual-function genotype of this entry, and dendritic abnormality is not cell loss.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 9 years, a brain MRI showed atrophy of the vermis and lateral hemispheres of the cerebellum that worsened at the age of 14 years, but without signs of demyelination or neuronal migration defects in forebrain and cerebellum
evidence.explanation: Establishes all three claims of this node at once: the anatomy, the progression between two scans, and the absence of both demyelination and the migration defect of classic Zellweger syndrome.

evidence.snippet: The patients that we describe seem to have progressive cerebellar atrophy rather than malformative cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: The authors' distinction between a degenerative and a malformative process, carrying their own hedge. INDIRECT because it is an interpretation of serial imaging, not a pathological finding.

steps/7.description: Progressive loss of cerebellar tissue, radiologically atrophy of the vermis and the lateral hemispheres, and in the most affected patient of the cerebellar peduncles and bulbar olives as well. Two features distinguish it from the severe band: it is degenerative rather than malformative - the Sevin brothers had no neuronal migration defect - and it occurs without white-matter signal change, so this is not a leukodystrophy. Marked HYPOTHETICAL because the step from the metabolic lesion to cerebellar cell loss is not established in these patients. The Purkinje cell is recorded as the vulnerable cell type on the strength of the PEX2-null mouse, in which Purkinje dendritic arborization is abnormal; no human PEX2 neuropathology is available, so the cell-level localisation is an inference from the model rather than an observation in these patients.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' description of the band this entry occupies, and the source of the organ set this node names. It is a statement about the intermediate and milder Zellweger spectrum as a whole rather than about PEX2, which is why the node is curated at spectrum level and why its non-sensory organ involvements carry no observed PEX2 instance.

steps/8.description: The organ-level consequences the peroxisomal lesion produces outside the nervous system - liver disease, adrenal insufficiency, renal oxalate stones, enamel and bone involvement. This node is curated at spectrum level rather than at PEX2 level, and the distinction is deliberate: the liver, adrenal, renal, enamel and bone features are not reported in a PEX2 mild-band patient in any source cited here, and the reason they belong in this entry is that GeneReviews describes them for the intermediate and milder band and builds its surveillance schedule around them. The sensory losses are different - hypoacusia and early retinopathy were both observed in the Italian PEX2 adult - so for those two downstream targets the node records an observed phenotype. For the rest, a reader should treat it as the expected organ set to watch for.

evidence.snippet: Two brothers are described who developed progressive cerebellar ataxia at 3 1/2 and 18 years, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Both the age range and the progressive course recorded on this binding, in the founding report of the presentation.

evidence.snippet: Cerebellar ataxia exacerbated slowly up to the age of 14 years but he was still able to walk without support.
evidence.explanation: The rate of progression in the younger brother, quoted because "slowly progressive" is a claim the entry makes repeatedly and this is the sentence that measures it.

steps/9.description: Cerebellar ataxia, the presenting and dominant feature of this entry's better documented subtype. Onset is in childhood in two of the three reported patients - three and a half years in one brother, three years in the Italian patient - and in adolescence in the third, at eighteen. Progression is slow enough that the brothers were walking unaided at fourteen and the Italian patient was ambulant at fifty-one.

evidence.snippet: Brain MRI revealed marked atrophy of the subtentorial regions including cerebellum, cerebellar peduncles, and bulbar olives, and showed moderate atrophy of the supratentorial regions of the brain
evidence.explanation: The fullest description of the imaging phenotype, in the oldest reported patient. Note that it extends beyond the cerebellum, which the younger patients' scans did not.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 9 years, a brain MRI showed atrophy of the vermis and lateral hemispheres of the cerebellum that worsened at the age of 14 years, but without signs of demyelination or neuronal migration defects in forebrain and cerebellum
evidence.explanation: Serial imaging in the same child, which is the basis for the PROGRESSIVE course on this binding rather than an inference from the clinical course.

steps/10.description: Cerebellar atrophy on MRI, in the reported patients involving the vermis and the lateral hemispheres and, in the oldest, the cerebellar peduncles and bulbar olives. White matter is spared, which is the imaging finding that separates this entry from the leukodystrophic presentations of the spectrum.

evidence.snippet: His milestones were normal but mild dysarthria was noticed at 2 1/2 years.
evidence.explanation: The earliest recorded sign in any patient in this entry, and the pediatric point that normal early milestones do not exclude it.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: An unrelated adult patient with the same sign.

steps/11.description: Cerebellar dysarthria. In the younger brother it was the first noticed sign, at about two and a half years, a year before the gait disturbance.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: The examination finding in the reported adult patient.

steps/12.description: Limb dysmetria, part of the cerebellar syndrome in both reported families.

evidence.snippet: On admission to our Department, neurological examination showed gait ataxia, lateral and vertical gaze-evoked nystagmus, hypoacusia, mild dysarthria, slight dysmetria, generalized areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: The oculomotor findings in the adult patient.

evidence.snippet: He had truncal ataxia, moderate cerebellar tremor, mild scanning dysarthria, nystagmus, slow saccades without oculo-motor apraxia and hyporeflexia.
evidence.explanation: The same sign in an unrelated child, with the explicit note that oculomotor apraxia was absent - the older brother's had it, so the sign is inconsistent within one family.

steps/13.description: Gaze-evoked nystagmus in the adult patient, and nystagmus with slow saccades in the younger of the two brothers. Reported with oculomotor apraxia in the older brother, which is a differential-diagnostic trap because it points towards the ataxias with oculomotor apraxia.

evidence.snippet: A 51-year-old Italian man was referred to us because of a clinical picture characterized by ataxia, areflexia, nystagmus, and strabismus, with childhood onset and slowly progressive course.
evidence.explanation: Areflexia named as one of the four cardinal features of the reported presentation.

steps/14.description: Generalised loss of tendon reflexes in the adult patient; hyporeflexia rather than areflexia in the two brothers. The combination of cerebellar ataxia with reduced reflexes is the clinical signature the reporting authors propose as the trigger for peroxisomal testing.

evidence.snippet: Nerve conduction studies indicated a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.explanation: The electrophysiological finding this binding records.

steps/15.description: Axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy on nerve conduction studies. It is not obligatory and it appears late: nerve conduction was normal in both brothers at nine, fourteen and eighteen years, and severe in the patient studied at fifty-one.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: The examination finding in the one patient in whom it is reported.

steps/16.description: Bilateral pes cavus in the adult patient with the severe axonal neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Between the third and the fifth decades, bilateral hypoacusia and initial retinopathy were detected.
evidence.explanation: The only PEX2-specific dating of the sensory loss in this entry, and the basis for calling it late and progressive rather than congenital.

evidence.snippet: Common to PBDs are liver disease, variable neurodevelopmental delay, retinopathy and perceptive deafness.
evidence.explanation: The class-level statement, quoted from the paper that reported the mildly affected complementation group 10 patient. It is a statement about peroxisome biogenesis disorders generally, not about this severity band, and is used only to place hearing loss among the expected features.

steps/17.description: Sensorineural hearing loss, which at this end of the spectrum is late and acquired rather than congenital: audiometry and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal in both brothers into the mid-teens, and hearing loss appeared in the Italian patient between the third and fifth decades. It is deliberately left unscoped by subtype, because it belongs both to the ataxic form on the strength of that patient and to the neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy / infantile Refsum presentation on the strength of the spectrum-general literature.

evidence.snippet: Between the third and the fifth decades, bilateral hypoacusia and initial retinopathy were detected.
evidence.explanation: The PEX2-specific observation, and the reason the binding carries a progressive course.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' account of sensory loss in the band this entry occupies. Spectrum-general rather than PEX2-specific, and marked OTHER because GeneReviews is an expert synthesis rather than a primary study.

steps/18.description: Retinopathy, also late in the ataxic form: fundoscopy and electroretinography were normal in both brothers at nine and fourteen years, and retinopathy was first detected in the Italian patient between the third and fifth decades. Like the hearing loss, it is left unscoped by subtype.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' description of the band this subtype occupies. It is a statement about the intermediate and milder Zellweger spectrum as a whole, not about PEX2, and no PEX2 patient in the sources cited here is reported with this feature - which is why the record is scoped to the NALD-IRD subtype and carries no frequency.

steps/19.description: Liver disease, which across the Zellweger spectrum ranges from raised transaminases and coagulopathy to fibrosis and cirrhosis. It is not reported in any of the three PEX2 mild-band patients curated here - liver enzymes were explicitly normal in the younger of the two ataxic brothers - so this record states an expected complication of the band rather than an observed PEX2 feature.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' description of the band this subtype occupies. It is a statement about the intermediate and milder Zellweger spectrum as a whole, not about PEX2, and no PEX2 patient in the sources cited here is reported with this feature - which is why the record is scoped to the NALD-IRD subtype and carries no frequency.

steps/20.description: Adrenocortical insufficiency. As with the liver disease, this is the band-level expectation that drives surveillance - annual ACTH and cortisol from the first year of life - and not an observed finding in any PEX2 mild-band patient cited here.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' description of the band this subtype occupies. It is a statement about the intermediate and milder Zellweger spectrum as a whole, not about PEX2, and no PEX2 patient in the sources cited here is reported with this feature - which is why the record is scoped to the NALD-IRD subtype and carries no frequency.

steps/21.description: Renal stones of calcium oxalate, reflecting loss of the peroxisomal glyoxylate detoxification that is also lost in primary hyperoxaluria type 1. Band-level rather than PEX2-observed; it is the reason an annual urine oxalate-to-creatinine ratio belongs in the surveillance schedule of a child with this diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Sensorineural deafness and ocular abnormalities like retinopathy, cataracts and glaucoma are typical
evidence.explanation: The management review's statement that cataract is a typical ocular finding of the spectrum, which is why it is carried as a surveillance target. The quote is trimmed at a line break in the cached full text; the same sentence goes on to warn that these findings are not always recognised at first presentation. INDIRECT because it is a spectrum-level statement and no PEX2 patient cited here is reported with cataract.

steps/22.description: Lens opacity, one of the ocular abnormalities the Zellweger spectrum management literature groups with retinopathy and glaucoma as typical and often missed at first presentation. Band-level rather than PEX2-observed; it is recorded because it is part of the ophthalmologic examination a child with this diagnosis is entered into surveillance for.

evidence.snippet: Some have osteopenia; almost all have ameleogenesis imperfecta in the secondary teeth.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' frequency statement for the band, quoted with its own misspelling intact because a snippet does not correct its source. The frequency is band-level and is not transferred to PEX2 as a rate.

steps/23.description: Defective enamel of the secondary dentition, which GeneReviews reports in almost all individuals in this band. It is the one feature of the multisystem set that is described as near-universal rather than variable, and it is the reason six-monthly dental review sits in the surveillance schedule. Not reported in any PEX2 patient cited here.

evidence.snippet: Some have osteopenia; almost all have ameleogenesis imperfecta in the secondary teeth.
evidence.explanation: The same sentence, quoted for the weaker of its two frequency claims. Recording both from one sentence keeps the contrast the source draws.

steps/24.description: Reduced bone mineral density, reported in some individuals in this band. GeneReviews contrasts it explicitly with the enamel defect - "some" against "almost all" - so the two are not equally expected. Not reported in any PEX2 patient cited here.

evidence.snippet: While hypotonia and developmental delays are typical, intellect can be normal.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews' statement for the intermediate and milder band, quoted whole so the qualifier travels with the claim: hypotonia and delay are typical, and preserved intellect is still compatible with the diagnosis.

steps/25.description: Hypotonia, which GeneReviews calls typical for the band together with developmental delay. It is absent from the PEX2 ataxic patients, whose early milestones were normal, which is the distinction between the two subtypes of this entry.

evidence.snippet: While hypotonia and developmental delays are typical, intellect can be normal.
evidence.explanation: The band-level statement. Its second clause is the one that matters for this entry: preserved intellect does not exclude the diagnosis, which is exactly what the PEX2 ataxic patients show.

evidence.snippet: Common to PBDs are liver disease, variable neurodevelopmental delay, retinopathy and perceptive deafness.
evidence.explanation: The class-level statement from the paper reporting the mildly affected complementation group 10 patient. It covers peroxisome biogenesis disorders generally, and the word "variable" is the operative one.

steps/26.description: Developmental delay, typical of the band but not of the ataxic subtype of this entry, whose patients had normal milestones and full-scale IQs in or near the normal range. Recorded so the two subtypes are not read as one.

evidence.snippet: The fact that peroxisomes in the patient's fibroblasts were normally present and contained catalase suggests that the mutated PEX2 is localized correctly in the peroxisomal membrane and still is partly active.
evidence.explanation: The authors' inference that the mild allele yields a partly active, correctly localised protein. Their own "suggests" is preserved and the item is marked INDIRECT, because the claim is read off organelle morphology rather than from an activity measurement.

edges/1.description: A residual-function PEX2 allele yields a peroxin-2 that reaches the peroxisomal membrane and retains part of its activity, rather than a protein that is absent or non-functional.

evidence.snippet: we noted the E55K mutation had mosaic activities of peroxisomal protein import machinery and residual activities of peroxisomal functions, including dihydroxyacetone phosphate acyltransferase and beta oxidation of very long chain fatty acids
evidence.explanation: The transfection experiment that ties a specific mild PEX2 allele to mosaic import and residual pathway activity, which is exactly what this edge asserts.

edges/2.description: Degraded ligase activity slows PEX5 recycling, so matrix-protein import is reduced rather than abolished - the state that produces a mixed population of import-competent and import-incompetent organelles.

evidence.snippet: The nonsense mutation severely affects these peroxisomal functions as well as the protein import.
evidence.explanation: The contrast that makes this edge quantitative rather than qualitative: in the same assay the null allele abolished the functions the mild allele preserved in part.

edges/3.description: Because the import defect is partial, the peroxisomal pathways run at reduced rather than absent capacity - and in the ataxic patients several of them measure normal in cultured fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: Further studies showed a moderate increase of bile acid intermediates (DHCA and THCA) in plasma and normal levels of pipecolic acid in plasma and CSF
evidence.explanation: The accumulating species measured in patients of the ataxic form, and the one that did not accumulate.

edges/4.description: Reduced alpha- and beta-oxidation capacity lets phytanic acid, pristanic acid and the C27 bile-acid intermediates DHCA and THCA rise in plasma, even where the very-long-chain fatty acids do not.

evidence.snippet: In our patient, the moderate impairment in peroxisome biogenesis affects predominantly neuronal cells in the cerebellum.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement of the tissue selectivity this edge asserts. Marked INDIRECT because it is read off the imaging and the clinical picture; the step from the accumulating metabolites to Purkinje-cell loss is not demonstrated in these patients, and the Sevin report says in as many words that how the defect selectively injures cerebellar neurons is unknown.

edges/5.description: The clinically dominant consequence at this end of the spectrum falls on the cerebellum. The link is an inference from the imaging and neuropathological pattern rather than a demonstrated toxic mechanism in these patients.

evidence.snippet: The moderate impairment in peroxisome biogenesis seems to affect predominantly neuronal cells in cerebellum, leading to cerebellar atrophy.
evidence.explanation: Ties the cerebellar tissue lesion to the clinical syndrome in a PEX2 patient. The authors' "seems to" is preserved.

edges/6.description: The cerebellar atrophy is the substrate of the ataxia that defines this entry's commonest presentation.

evidence.snippet: Brain MRI showed marked cerebellar atrophy and absence of white matter involvement.
evidence.explanation: The imaging finding in a PEX2 patient, together with the negative that keeps this entry out of the leukodystrophies.

edges/7.description: The radiological expression of the same tissue lesion.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: The cerebellar examination findings in the reported adult patient.

edges/8.description: Cerebellar dysarthria, reported in patients of both families.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: Records the dysmetria alongside the other cerebellar signs in the patient with marked cerebellar atrophy on MRI.

edges/9.description: Limb dysmetria, a cerebellar sign of the same lesion.

evidence.snippet: On admission to our Department, neurological examination showed gait ataxia, lateral and vertical gaze-evoked nystagmus, hypoacusia, mild dysarthria, slight dysmetria, generalized areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: Names the nystagmus as gaze-evoked, which is what places it with the cerebellar lesion rather than with the retinopathy.

edges/10.description: Gaze-evoked nystagmus, an oculomotor sign of the cerebellar lesion.

evidence.snippet: Electromyography and nerve conduction studies indicated a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.explanation: The examination and electrophysiology behind this phenotype.

edges/11.description: The clinical and electrophysiological expression of the axonal lesion.

evidence.snippet: On admission to our Department, neurological examination showed gait ataxia, lateral and vertical gaze-evoked nystagmus, hypoacusia, mild dysarthria, slight dysmetria, generalized areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus. Electromyography and nerve conduction studies indicated a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Puts the generalised areflexia and the axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy in the same patient on the same examination, which is the closest the sources come to the causal step. INDIRECT because co-occurrence in one patient does not establish that the neuropathy produced the areflexia, and because the separately reported Sevin brothers had reduced reflexes with normal nerve conduction.

edges/12.description: Generalised loss of tendon reflexes. The neuropathy explains it in only one of the three reported PEX2 patients: the Italian adult had generalised areflexia alongside a severe axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy on nerve conduction studies, whereas both Sevin brothers already had reduced reflexes while their nerve conduction remained normal at nine and fourteen years. In those two the hyporeflexia preceded any demonstrable neuropathy, so this edge is the mechanism in the adult and not an established explanation for the sign wherever it appears in this entry.

evidence.snippet: Neurological examination revealed gait ataxia, dysarthria, dysmetria, areflexia, and bilateral pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: Records the pes cavus alongside the areflexia in the same patient. INDIRECT because the source states the co-occurrence, not the causal step from denervation to foot deformity.

edges/13.description: The skeletal consequence of long-standing distal denervation, present bilaterally in the one patient in whom the neuropathy was severe.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of functional peroxisomes, bile acid synthesis is disrupted, and multisystem disease ensues with abnormalities in the brain, liver, kidneys, muscle, eyes, ears, and nervous system.
evidence.explanation: Names disrupted bile-acid synthesis as the step between the peroxisomal lesion and multisystem disease including the liver. INDIRECT, and stated for absent peroxisomes rather than for the partial import defect of this entry.

edges/14.description: Liver involvement, the organ problem the one approved therapy is directed at.

evidence.snippet: ACTH and cortisol levels by age one year and annually thereafter.
evidence.explanation: The surveillance interval, quoted because it is the actionable form of this claim. INDIRECT: it establishes that the risk is expected in this band, not that any PEX2 patient has developed it.

edges/15.description: Adrenocortical failure, which GeneReviews asks to be screened for from age one.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the sensory loss of this band to progressive peroxisome dysfunction. INDIRECT: the mechanism between the metabolic lesion and cochlear failure is not stated, and the sentence is spectrum-level rather than PEX2-specific.

edges/16.description: Progressive sensorineural hearing loss, one of the two sensory losses GeneReviews names for this band. In the one PEX2 patient followed long enough it appeared in adult life.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with intermediate/milder ZSD do not have congenital malformations, but rather progressive peroxisome dysfunction variably manifest as sensory loss (secondary to retinal dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss), neurologic involvement (ataxia, polyneuropathy, and leukodystrophy), liver dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and renal oxalate stones.
evidence.explanation: The same sentence, for the retinal half of the sensory loss. INDIRECT for the same reasons.

edges/17.description: Retinal dystrophy, the second of the two sensory losses, and likewise late at this locus.

evidence.snippet: Sensorineural deafness and ocular abnormalities like retinopathy, cataracts and glaucoma are typical
evidence.explanation: Places cataract among the typical ocular findings of the Zellweger spectrum, alongside the retinopathy and deafness this node already carries edges for. INDIRECT because the statement is about the spectrum rather than about PEX2, and because no intermediate step between the peroxisomal lesion and the lens is given.

edges/18.description: Lens opacity, which the management review groups with retinopathy and glaucoma as the typical ocular involvement of the spectrum. Band-level, like the retinal dystrophy edge above, and not observed in a PEX2 patient in any source cited here.

evidence.snippet: Some have osteopenia; almost all have ameleogenesis imperfecta in the secondary teeth.
evidence.explanation: Places the enamel defect in this band and gives its frequency there. INDIRECT: no mechanism linking the peroxisomal lesion to amelogenesis is stated, and no PEX2 patient is reported with it.

edges/19.description: Enamel defect of the secondary dentition, the most consistently reported non-neurological feature of this band.

evidence.snippet: Some have osteopenia; almost all have ameleogenesis imperfecta in the secondary teeth.
evidence.explanation: The weaker of the two frequency claims in that sentence, recorded so the contrast the source draws is preserved on the edge as well as on the phenotype.

edges/20.description: Reduced bone mineral density, reported in some individuals in this band.

evidence.snippet: While hypotonia and developmental delays are typical, intellect can be normal.
evidence.explanation: The band-level expectation. INDIRECT, and quoted with its qualifier so the edge does not read as a claim that every patient in this entry is hypotonic.

edges/21.description: Hypotonia, typical of this band but absent from the PEX2 ataxic patients, whose early development was normal.

evidence.snippet: While hypotonia and developmental delays are typical, intellect can be normal.
evidence.explanation: The same band-level sentence, whose second clause is the one that matters here: preserved intellect does not exclude the diagnosis.

edges/22.description: Developmental delay, typical of this band and absent from the ataxic subtype of this entry.

evidence.snippet: Annual urine oxalate-to-creatinine ratio with consideration of kidney imaging when performing liver imaging.
